correctness.rationale: For divisible scalar-block multiplicities explicit residue interleaving yields exact kth roots. For the mixed nondivisible case the Calkin midpoint resolvent has inverse norm precisely 2/|a-b| and Fredholm index equal to the negative outer-block multiplicity. A perturbation smaller than half the scale separation preserves the index on the entire separating circle, while factorization of a kth power forces index divisibility by k. The midpoint merged-scale kth power has matching norm and essential norm. Cases a=b, both orders, and all integer boundary conditions were addressed analytically.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the exact quantitative norm and essential-norm distance for two constant-scale direct sums and all orders k, rather than existence of roots or a general qualitative characterization of their norm closure. Full public HTML of the 2022 weighted-shift paper and accessible text of the 2021 classical-root preprint were inspected. The 1987 norm-closure theorem is explicitly acknowledged and its uninspected full paper is a significant historical-priority risk. Six targeted mathematical-index searches returned no equivalent exact gap or stronger quantitative formula. The same slot's available 98 earlier claims contained no two-scale k-th-power distance theorem.
residual_risks: Full 1987 Conway–Morrel paper was not accessible; it might contain a specialized quantitative distance estimate not visible in the abstract.
Semantic indexing is non-exhaustive and cannot establish global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Sharp quantitative stabilization of kth-root nonexistence under arbitrary bounded perturbations and even modulo compacts. The exact scale-sensitive gap, matching minimizer, and all-order multiplicity dichotomy make the problem a complete natural model calculation rather than an ad hoc special case; the result is useful for testing perturbation robustness of algebraic operator properties. Qualitative Fredholm obstruction alone does not yield the number.
